title: Nvidia Launches Open Source OpenShell to Secure AI Agents
summary:
Jensen Huang revealed a system at GTC Berlin that enables companies to block AI agents from unauthorized networks and files. The OpenShell Reference Architecture is an open source framework that uses hardware-isolated security and a policy prover to mathematically verify resource access. By blocking all actions by default, the architecture ensures agents operate within secure sandboxes and can be hosted on a company's own infrastructure to keep sensitive code and data internal.

The framework integrates with Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents, which is currently in public beta. While Anthropic handles the orchestration of the agents, Nvidia provides the execution environment and security controls. This combined approach allows businesses to deploy agentic AI at scale using runtime controls that monitor and log every permitted or blocked action.

selectedTweets.text:
Jensen Huang just showed how NVIDIA and Anthropic are working together to make AI agents more secure with $NVDA OpenShell and Claude Managed Agents.

OpenShell allows AI agents to operate inside secure sandboxes while controlling exactly what they can access and do.

Here's how it works:

• Controls which files, tools, networks, and private data AI agents can access.

• Blocks actions by default unless explicitly permitted by security policies.

• Monitors agent activity and logs every allowed or blocked action.

• Allows companies to run agent execution inside their own infrastructure, keeping sensitive data and code within their environment.

• Uses a policy prover to mathematically verify what resources an agent can access.

With Claude Managed Agents, Anthropic handles agent orchestration while NVIDIA OpenShell adds security controls inside the execution environment.

NVIDIA OpenShell is open source, while Claude Managed Agents is available in public beta.
